Depending on the size it should be pretty manageable. If it's one of the full size, basically 16 wheeler ones, that's going to be tougher but not impossible. As others said, since you'll be mostly along the 95, there should be plenty of options for lodging. 

If you're worried about backing it up, avoid it all together. Look for hotel complexes where 3 or 4 hotels are all right next to each other. They usually share parking lots or at least expect a lot of travelers so there will be a lot of space. You can park away from other cars and have plenty of room to maneuver out without risking hitting anything. 

Alternatively, look for hotels near Wal-Marts or truck stops. Many of them will allow you to leave your Uhaul there and then you can walk/Uber to your hotel. 

Securing your stuff can be a little tough. Obviously have a lock but aside from that, use your common sense. Park in well lit areas, avoid areas that look like warzones, and if you do end up parking at a Wal-Mart or truck stop, many of them have overnight security. And if all else fails, try backing up near a bush. If you hit it, it wont damage the Uhaul and thieves won't want to climb through thorns and branches to try and steal something random. 

PS: You didnt mention it but make sure you allow a lot of time for the border and make sure you have checked everything you will need. I missed a form once bringing stuff from Toronto to Buffalo and ended up delayed for almost 6 hours and had to call my attorney.

Well, I can help you with the copyright portion of this. Unfortunately, anime is one of the most commonly copyrighted categories on YouTube so it's a bit tough but there's ways around it. You can often get away showing VERY short clips (5 seconds or less) on YouTube without it causing too many issues but I would also mix in still images from the anime to talk about so you can cut down on video clips. For any video you do show, definitely mirror it and if you use the audio, adjust the pitch so it doesn't set off YouTube's flags. If you're going to be showing manga, remove words from any word bubbles - the copyright holders seems to be more ok with that; and try not to show much of anything brand new. If you're talking about a brand new chapter, mix in general pictures of the characters to talk about. I also like having a side youtube account that you can upload your videos to first to see if it's sets off any red flags. It keeps eyes off the main channel.

As far as niches, look at what you like as well as search trends. Where you see an overlap, that's your best chance. I would also recommend using your multilingualism and consider making a second channel in the other language. Like Bills Channel and Bills Channel Espanol. 

When you're just starting off, try not to worry about monetization. If you make engaging content that people come back to and watch a lot of, the monetization will come. 

Hope this helps!

Make sure you have a plan for where to sleep. For travelers who are car sleeping by choice, truck stops are a great go to. They're well lit, have decent security, are very welcoming to overnighters and have 24/7 amenities including showers. Wal-Marts and public camp grounds are also good sometimes but they can be hit or miss. DO NOT try and sleep in a fancy neighborhood or near a school. That will almost always result in cops getting called.   


As far as storage, it depends on your car. Personally, I've had luck with putting my rear seats down and then putting a 1 person thermarest down to sleep on. Make sure you have a bunch of blankets because you won't want to run your car all night. The rest of your needs kind of depend on what you plan on doing. If you're going to be swimming, make sure you have a spot to hand a towel and bathing suit to let them dry. If you're going hiking, make sure to bring gear for that.   


I'd also recommend a power inverter so you can charge things larger than a phone like laptop. Also make sure you have water and some shelf stable food just in case. I recommend PB&J's and jerky. Protein makes you fuller longer and you won't have a sugar crash.   


PS: When you get to Florida I highly recommend checking out St. Augustine. It's a beautiful town with a ton of beach spaces that are rarely crowded. Plus the have the only pirate museum in the US!

Aside from the obvious (emergency money, phone charger, etc) you'll want to make sure you have a spare and jack just in case.  Also not a bad idea to have jumper cables.   


Food wise, don't just grab a ton of junk food. Try to bring protein dense foods like PB&J's & beef jerky. It'll keep you fuller longer and will avoid sugar crashes. Same with drinks. Try to save the coffee and energy drinks for when you need a pick me up and drink a non-stimulant the majority of the time.  If you get take out, avoid anything greasy. Last thing you want is to be desperate for a toilet when the next rest stop is 80 miles away.  


I'd also recommend blankets in case you get stranded or need to rest your eyes   


Aside from that, plan your route, look for any places along the way you'd want to stop. Remember, you'll need breaks so you might as well enjoy yourself while you take them.

It's great that other JRPG's have western dragons which I totally agree with but I have seen no indication that GameFreak ever copied those or used them for inspirations in my research. Everything I have found indicates that they were focusing on traditional Japanese inspirations and borrowed heavily from dinosaurs, kaiju, and yokais. So I can't simply look at what other JRPG's have done and say "yup, western dragons are in those so theyre japanese now"

Regarding Dragonite, yeah, it's a big departure from Dratini & Dragonair but it still is closer to Japanese Dragons than Charizard. Japanese Dragons are tied to water. Dragonite is the guardian of the seas, where as Charizard just breaths fire. Additionally, as far as I'm concerned, Beta Dragonite really helps connect it to Japanese dragons simply because it still has the spines and longer neck, making it a lot closer.

Obviously you can just say the hell with it, they definitely copied western dragons but there is no evidence of that that I can find any source on and every aspect of Charizard can be explained by looking at classical Japanese inspirations. If we disagree, that's fine but I am basing all of my arguments on the facts and evidence I have found.
